title: Relationship Model
description: A traversable link between two catalog entities. Relationships are what make the platform's two hardest capabilities possible: graph expansion during AI retrieval (a user says 'security', the retriever also offers pricing and related parties), and declarative data traversal without the author writing a join.

id.description: Qualified id owned by the 'from' entity, e.g. 'securities.security.related-parties'.

businessName.description: How the link reads to a business user — 'Related Parties', 'Latest Price', 'Raised By'. Used verbatim in generated tab titles and section headings.

inverseId.description: The relationship representing the same link in the opposite direction. Required for graph expansion to traverse without duplicating edges.

keyMapping.description: Logical attribute pairs joining the two entities. Attribute ids, never physical columns.

throughEntity.description: Associative entity for many-to-many links, whose own attributes may carry meaning (a holding's quantity, an override's reason).

joinSemantics.description: 'inner' drops rows with no match; 'left' preserves them. Wrong here, a dashboard silently under-reports — so it is a catalog decision made once by a steward rather than a per-page choice.

temporalSemantics.description: How the link resolves over time for effective-dated entities. 'latest' takes the most recent related instance (latest price); 'asOfParent' matches the parent's effective date; 'all' returns the full history.

navigable.description: False blocks traversal in data sources — used where a link exists conceptually but querying it is prohibitively expensive.

traversalCost.description: Bounds graph expansion during AI retrieval and traversal depth in data sources, so a highly-connected entity cannot pull in the whole catalog or the whole database.

expectedFanout.description: Typical number of related instances per parent. Informs whether the AI should generate a tab, an inline list, or a count.

relationshipEntitlement.description: Optional entitlement key gating traversal itself, for cases where the existence of a link is sensitive even when both entities are visible.
